THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 01.06.2019 passed in MVC No.3412/2018 by XV Additional Small Causes Judge & XXIII A.C.M.M.
Member, MACT, Bengaluru (for short 'the tribunal').

XV Additional Small Causes Judge & XXIII A.C.M.M.
Member, MACT, Bengaluru

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.

2. Brief facts of the case:
The claimant was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-04/JB-3504 on Hesaraghatta road on 09.03.2018, when he reached near Black and White Dhaba,
Hurulichikkanahalli, at that time, a private bus bearing registration No.KA-14/A-2920 driven by its driver in a rash NC: 2024:KHC:2209 and negligent manner in order to endanger human life and safety, dashed against the vehicle of the claimant.
Due to which, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Sapthagiri hospital, where he administered first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Manipal hospital and again for better treatment,
he was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah hospital, where he took treatment as an inpatient for a period of 56 days on intermediary occasions and expended more than a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, transport and other charges.

3. It is the case of the claimant that prior to the occurrence of the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was pursuing 2nd year Electrical Diploma in Acharya Diploma College and due to the negligence of the driver of the bus, he sustained injuries and encountered permanent disability,

sentences.text: Due to the occurrence of the accident, a crime is registered against the driver of the bus in Cr.No.33/2019 for the offences NC: 2024:KHC:2209 punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC.
Due to the injuries sustained and loss of financial income and mental agony, he preferred a claim petition against the respondents.
3.1. The respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal and filed statement of objections, whereas the respondent No.2 was placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.1/insurance company denied the averments made in the claim petition including, age, avocation, income, injuries sustained and negligence attributed to the driver of the bus.
It was further pleaded that the claimant was a minor as on the date of occurrence of the accident and was not possessing a valid driving licence.

Hence,
question of awarding any compensation to the claimant is farfetched.
It is also pleaded that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the claimant, who was not holding proper licence and was incapable of riding two wheeler.
On these grounds, he sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.2. On the basis of pleading, tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

In order to substantiate the issues and to prove the case, the claimant examined himself as PW.1 and three other witnesses as PWs.2 to 4 in support of his case and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P32.
On the contrary, the respondent No.1 neither lead any evidence nor produced any documents.

4. On the basis of both oral and documentary evidence, the tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.12,18,771/- and attributed contributory negligence to an extent of 10% against the claimant and after deducting the said amount, compensation of a sum of Rs.10,97,000/- was directed to be paid by respondent No.1/insurance company with interest at 9% per annum, from the date of petition till realization.
The compensation amount was directed to be paid within 60 days from the date of the award.

5. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the tribunal committed serious error in not awarding suitable compensation under several heads including assessment of income as the claimant suffered serious injuries leading to the disability and loss of NC:
2024:KHC:2209 future earning capacity.

It is further contended by the learned counsel that under other heads also, the tribunal has awarded meager compensation even though considering the evidence of the claimant with regard to loss of academic year due to the injuries sustained in the accident and having not attended the classes.
It is also contended that under the head loss of amenities and future medical expenses, the tribunal has awarded meager compensation, which calls for interference.
On these grounds, the learned counsel seeks to allow this appeal and consequently enhance the compensation.

6. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.1/insurance company vehemently contended that the tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation to the claimant, who is a minor student studying in the 2nd year Electrical Diploma and has continued to pursue his course and as on date of adducing his evidence, he was in the 4th year of his Electrical Diploma.

He has also disputed that Namilla Girish Kumar Reddy vs The Manager on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32036855/
3 the injuries having caused disturbance in his course of study and having lost the academic year, the compensation awarded is NC: 2024:KHC:2209 on the higher side.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the insurance company also contends that in the case of minor child, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future earning capacity would not arise, but as in the present case, the claimant is a student and continued his education from the 2nd year and as on date of adducing evidence, he was in the 4th year of his Electrical Diploma, utmost the claimant would have lost few classes, but has not discontinued the education and has continued the education.

It is also contended by the learned counsel for the insurance company that it had filed an appeal prior to claimant's appeal in MFA No.6191/2019 and the same came to be withdrawn by the insurance company vide order dated 18.02.2020.
He contended that insurance company has withdrawn the appeal on the premise that the compensation awarded to the claimant is just and reasonable and therefore, they have not pursued the appeal.
On these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal as the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is just and reasonable.
Infact on the contrary, he contends that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the higher side.

I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.1.
8.

I have perused the impugned judgment and award and it is seen that there is no dispute with regard to the occurrence of the accident that on 09.03.2018 while the claimant was riding his motorcycle, he was hit by a private bus which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner.
In order to establish this aspect, the claimant has produced Exs.P1 to P32.
Exs. P1

to P7 are the police records, wherein FIR has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle and the charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the bus which was not questioned or challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to establish the injuries suffered and the medical expenses expended by the claimant, the documents at Exs.P9 to P32 are produced which evidenced the fact that the claimant has expended huge amount towards medical treatment due to the injuries suffered in the road traffic NC: 2024:KHC:2209 accident arising out of the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
9. It is also admitted that the claimant was a minor as on the date of occurrence of the accident and he was aged 17 years.
There is no document produced to show that he possessed a valid driving licence to ride the motorcycle.

The tribunal on the basis of the material evidence placed on record and the submission of learned counsel for both the parties, and on consideration of evidence of doctor PW.2, has assessed the disability to an extent of 20% to the whole body and taken the income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month as notional income.
Considering the fact that the claimant was aged 17 years, calculated the multiplier at '18' and awarded loss of future earning at Rs.2,59,200/-.
10. A sum of Rs.80,000/- was awarded towards pain and suffering,

towards medical expenses a sum of Rs.6,94,571/- was awarded, towards transportation, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges a sum of Rs.45,000/- was awarded, towards loss of future income Namilla Girish Kumar Reddy vs The Manager on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32036855/

sentences.text: due to permanent disability that is to an extent of 20%, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,59,200/-.

Towards loss of income during laid up period, a sum of Rs.50,000/- and a sum of Rs.50,000/- was awarded towards future medical expenses, a sum of Rs.50,000/- was awarded towards loss of academic year and a sum of Rs.40,000/- was awarded towards loss of amenities.
11. On perusal of the impugned judgment and award, I do not find any error committed by the tribunal in awarding compensation to the claimant.
Admittedly, the claimant was a minor at the time of accident and did not possess a valid driving licence.
Accordingly, the tribunal held contributory negligence as against the rider of the motorcycle i.e., claimant at 10%.
I do not find any need to interfere with the same and same is retained.

12. With regard to compensation awarded by the tribunal under several heads also, this Court does not find any error apparent on the face of the record or contrary to the settled principles of law formulated time and again by this Court and the Hon'ble Apex Court.
Nothing is placed on record before this Court by the learned counsel for both the parties either to enhance the compensation or to reduce the compensation.

The question of reducing the compensation would not arise as the respondent No.1/insurance company has neither filed any appeal nor it has filed any cross-objection objecting the appeal preferred by the claimant.

Therefore,
considering the fact that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, I do not find any need to interfere with the judgment.

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed and the impugned judgment and award passed in MVC No.3412/2018 dated 01.06.2019 by the XV Additional Small Causes Judge & XXIII ACMM,
Member, MACT, Bengaluru is affirmed.
